title: Sriram Dang v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: R.K. Agrawal, J.; Mushaffey Ahmad, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; Clause 4.4 application to be decided in a week.
headnote: On a second writ after the landlady cut supply and a Clause 4.4 application under the 2005 Code sat undecided for over two and a half months, the Division Bench directed the competent authority to pass an appropriate order in accordance with law within a week of a certified copy being filed, expressly without deciding the petitioner's claim on merits.
facts: The landlady disconnected the petitioner's electricity. He first obtained an order dated 23 February 2012 in Writ-C No. 7909 of 2012 directing him to apply under Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He applied on 28 February 2012. After more than two and a half months with no decision, he filed this second writ. The Court directed respondent no. 2 to decide the application in accordance with law within a week, without ruling on merits.

holding_units.holding: A pending Clause 4.4 application for a new connection, left undecided for more than two and a half months after an earlier High Court direction to apply, is to be decided by the competent authority in accordance with law within a week of a certified copy being filed; the Court did not adjudicate entitlement on merits.

not_decided.point: Merits of the petitioner's claim to a new connection under Clause 4.4
not_decided.note: The Court expressly stated it had not adjudicated the petitioner's claim on merits.
